races.title: State Assembly, District 56
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Lisa Calderon
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 56 (Gateway Cities and part of the San Gabriel Valley), first elected in 2020. Previously Government Affairs Director at Edison International (1996–2020) and a legislative aide to Assembly Speaker Willie Brown (1990–1996). Has chaired the Human Services and Insurance committees.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia among her 2026 endorsements: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Calderon was born or raised, or when she came to California. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, and we found no questionnaire or interview stating her positions. The pages we had show no specific actions or stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, police funding, gun laws, abortion or school choice. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or statements on data centers or development.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Sitting Assemblymember since 2020, with seats on the Appropriations and Utilities and Energy committees. Earlier she was a legislative aide to Speaker Willie Brown (1990–1996) and Government Affairs Director at Edison International (1996–2020).
qual.why: She has prior legislative service plus long policy and government-affairs careers, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted.
qual.label: She has prior legislative service plus long policy and government-affairs careers, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

cands.name: Jessica Martinez
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 56 who has run for the seat or its predecessor (District 57) in 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2026. Former Whittier City Council member and Mayor Pro Tem. Educator with a law degree. Past employers include SCE, the federal government and public schools.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed for 2026 and 2024)

cands.gaps: We could not find where Jessica Martinez was born or raised, or the year she moved to Whittier. We also could not find the dates of her Whittier City Council service or her Mayor Pro Tem term, or any council votes or actions. Nothing in the sources covers her stance on data centers, housing or land development, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, or H-1B visas. We found no documented actions in office on any of these topics, only statements. Her campaign site offers no detail on teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2020 through 2026; the only survey answers are from 2018. No controversies, foreign ties or independent news coverage turned up in the pages available.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign site says she has lived in Whittier for more than 20 years; her birthplace, upbringing and arrival date are not given, so the score rests on the length of residence alone.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served on the Whittier City Council and as its Mayor Pro Tem, and holds a Juris Doctorate from Trinity Law School. Worked in communications at SCE, for the federal government and in public schools.
qual.why: Local elected office plus a law degree and educator background fits the middle band. She has no prior state legislative service or budget career, and board seats were not counted.
qual.label: Local elected office plus a law degree and educator background fits the middle band. She has no prior state legislative service or budget career, and board seats were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says she supports charter schools, vouchers and homeschooling options. Her site does not mention teacher pay.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says she is a proud supporter of Prop 13 and believes the limits it places on taxing agencies are appropriate. She also says she stands for lower taxes.

pro-life.evidence: Says she is pro-life and believes every life has purpose, is precious, and must be protected.

second-amendment.evidence: Says the right to life and to bear arms are important values and that the right to self-defense is essential.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she is committed to law and order and to supporting law enforcement.

workers-first.evidence: Says she supports securing the borders. In a 2018 Ballotpedia survey she listed ending the sanctuary state among her policy passions.

prio.label: Matches 6 of 6 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 6 only promised

roots.summary: Her campaign site says she has lived in Whittier for more than 20 years; her birthplace, upbringing and arrival date are not given, so the score rests on the length of residence alone.
